subject: Get wrong result when put the raw data which has colnames into HDFS

messages.author: 8f47194462f479af
messages.subject: Get wrong result when put the raw data which has colnames into HDFS
parts:
It is my code for test this problem:
hdfs.put("/home/jingmin/mytest.txt", "/home/jingmin/test/");
read <- function(k,v) {
  Hmy <- v;
  colnames(Hmy) <- paste("sam_", c(1: ncol(Hmy)), sep = "");
  write.table(Hmy, "/home/jingmin/ttt.txt", sep = "\t",quote=F);
  Hmy
}
contents <- mapreduce(
  input = "/home/jingmin/test/mytest.txt",
  output = "/home/jingmin/test/output",
  map=read,
  reduce=NULL,
  combine=NULL,
  input.format=make.input.format("csv",sep= "\t", row.names = 1),
  backend.parameters = list(hadoop = list(D = "mapred.map.tasks=4"))
)
)

My raw data have 3001 lines include colnames and its value just has 3 types(0, 1, 2) like figure 1. I didn't delete the colnames when I put the raw data file to HDFS.
The write.table part is OK which is executed in map like figure 2.
The problem is in the final result. I use look <- from.dfs(contents)$val to check the result and find like figure 3. Its value changed. There are not any value is 3 or 4 in my raw data, but the value which is 3 or 4 come out in the result. 
If I delete the colnames of raw data file and put into HDFS, it is OK, the result is right. But I wonder the reason of it happen when I didn't delete the colnames.  Thank you very much.

messages.author: 6ac7e7dfbe4f6c38
messages.subject: Re: [RHadoop:#1202] Get wrong result when put the raw data which has colnames into HDFS
parts:
Headers are not supported and the manual says as much. If you have any ideas as to supporting headers in a setting were file are arbitrarily partitioned, please share. That think of writing to a local file from the mapper is guaranteed to fail. At least you need attempt-unique names and you need to append in each map call. The fact that it works on a tiny dataset is deceptive, because there will be a single map call. What are you trying to do? You can have the whole job write out in csv format if that's needed.


Antonio
